oh_bell_ridge_boulders.blurb: A cluster of sandstone boulders in the hills north of Marietta, in the southeast corner of the state, strung out beside a small climbers' trail that runs for a few hundred yards. It is a pure bouldering spot with 28 problems, and the whole area sits within about half a mile of the trailhead. Grades start at the very easiest and stretch to the high end, with the bulk of the lines falling between V2 and V4 and a handful of harder tests above that. Expect a quiet, wooded setting with no cell coverage. The stone in this region is porous, so give it a day or two to dry after rain before pulling on holds.

oh_a_west_side_boulders.blurb: The westernmost sector of the Marne Road roadside crag near Hanover, in central Ohio. About 27 sandstone boulder problems are packed into a short stretch, ranging from V1 up into the V8 range, with the biggest share in the middle grades around V4 and a good number of V5 to V7 lines for stronger climbers. Styles vary: short steep problems, technical slabs and a few tall highballs, some with big flat landings and others that call for extra pads. Several lines stay dry most of the year, while others seep through winter and spring. The rock quality swings from solid to crumbly, so test holds. The walk in is short, and there are no facilities nearby.

_expect.name: Genesis Wall and East Side Boulders

oh_f_genesis_wall_and_east_side_boulders.blurb: The far end of the Marne Road crag near Hanover in central Ohio, mixing roped lines and bouldering on sandstone. The steep Genesis face holds some of the longest and hardest sport leads on the cliff, demanding pocket and crimp strength, with most of the ten sport routes in the 5.12 range and a few at 5.11 and 5.13. A single trad line is also here. Around the corner, 16 boulder problems run from about V2 to V8, mostly V5 and V6. The lower few feet of the wall can seep, particularly in spring, while the upper sections tend to stay drier. Rock quality is variable, and the wall catches morning sun.

oh_east_wall_the.blurb: A tall stone retaining wall of limestone columns in Eden Park, close to downtown Cincinnati, with a distinctive arch at its centre. It faces east and is regarded as the best of the park's four climbing spots. Most of the 26 lines are bouldering, running from the easiest grades up to about V7, with a handful of top-rope routes between 5.7 and 5.11 that make it a popular place for beginners to learn. Anchors can be built along the wall top. The bottom of the stone is slick and polished, landings are generally flat grass, and it takes a couple of days to dry after heavy rain. Skip highballs here unless you are confident.
oh_east_wall_the.parking_note: Drive in on Eden Park Drive and continue to Martin Drive. The wall stands right beside the road at the parking lot, so it is only a few steps from the car.

oh_upstream.blurb: One of the boulder sectors along Chippewa Creek in the gorge of Brecksville Reservation, south of Cleveland. About two dozen sandstone problems lie along the creek a short way above the drop-in, spanning from easy to very hard. The bulk sit between V2 and V5, with a few V6 to V7 lines and a couple of V9 projects for experts. The Berea sandstone and shale in the gorge turn fragile when wet, so wait several dry, breezy days after rain before climbing. Moss and lichen cover rarely used blocks, sandbars shift the starts, and summer weekends can be busy and buggy. Bring pads and a helmet.
